artifacts.summary: Settles the lease-vs-advisory question (bounded lease, mandatory fail-open on timeout) and designs gate-acquire/gate-release task-lock.sh subcommands wired into run-all.sh and verify-deploy.sh's gate8_run(), reusing acquire_named_mutex, resolve_session_pid, session_liveness, and the RUN_ALL_NESTED/VERIFY_DEPLOY_NESTED/COMMIT_MUTEX_HELD reentrancy patterns with no new concurrency primitive.

memory_candidates.content: task-lock.sh's acquire_named_mutex/release_named_mutex is a generic, repo-root-scoped, mkdir-atomic named-mutex primitive with holder-declared staleness and a bounded wait budget. It already backs .scope-lock, .commit-lock, and .contention-claims; any new cross-session coordination need in this codebase should be a new thin wrapper (new mutex dirname + constants + CLI subcommand pair) over this primitive, not a new concurrency mechanism. Fail-open-vs-fail-closed is a CALLER decision applied at the call site (see git-commit-scoped.sh's .commit-lock usage), never baked into the primitive, which always fails closed (returns nonzero) on timeout.

RUN_ALL_NESTED (tests/run-all.sh) and VERIFY_DEPLOY_NESTED (verify-deploy.sh) are an established, line-for-line-identical nested-invocation guard pattern: check an inherited env var, degrade behavior if already set, (re-)export it unconditionally so further nesting also degrades. COMMIT_MUTEX_HELD is the same idea applied to an actual held mutex (reentrancy flag, not a job-count cap) -- any new script that can be invoked both standalone and nested inside another instance of the gate-running machinery should reuse this exact three-part shape (check / degrade-or-skip / export) rather than inventing a new nesting signal.
